q1.answer: On the left side. The child was born with a split in the lip and gum on the left.

q2.answer: In the bone under the pink gum, in the bone that holds the teeth, on the upper jaw where the split is.

q3.answer: The small tooth next to the left front tooth is missing. About half of children with a cleft do not have it.

q4.answer: The eye tooth waits high in the bone and needs bone to grow into, so the graft gives it bone to come down into.

q7.answer: New bone fills the gap from the floor of the nose down to the gum and joins the two parts of the upper jaw. The gum has healed over it. The eye tooth is still in the bone and starts to move down.

q8.answer: With an X-ray, at about 3 to 6 months after the operation.

q9.answer: The hip can be sore for a while after surgery.

q10.answer: It has come down through the new bone into the row of teeth. Some get stuck and need a small operation.

q12.answer: Braces can move the eye tooth into the gap and the dentist reshapes it. Or keep the gap with a false tooth on a plate you can take out. Or, when you stop growing, an implant or a bridge. The cleft team helps you choose.
